# bugs #3687: mcs51: division and modulo of unsigned char by a constant call __divsint and __modsint

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/3687/

- Recommended action: Close as fixed in r14650. The longer increments of volatile objects are required, as the fifth comment explains.

## Finding

The source of the program is not in the ticket, so the size of the whole program on r17176 was not
measured. A file with the statements that the ticket and its comments show was compiled for mcs51
on r17176 with `--opt-code-size --model-small`. The declarations follow the listing attached to
the third comment, with `volatile uint8_t` objects and a table in code memory.

- `display_hour % 12`, `ledtable[hour / 10]`, `ledtable[hour % 10]`, and
  `ledtable[alarm_minute % 10]` use `div ab`. The file has no call of `__divsint` or `__modsint`.
- The table accesses use `mov dptr,#_ledtable` and `movc a,@a+dptr`. `ledtable[hour / 10]` takes 7
  instructions and `ledtable[alarm_minute % 10]` takes 8, as in the listing from 3.5.0.
- `if (--next_blink == 0)` takes 4 instructions. The listing from 4.4.0 has 5. The listing from
  3.5.0 has 3 and reads the volatile object twice.
- `if (++timer_second == 60)` takes 5 instructions, as in 4.4.0. The listing from 3.5.0 has 3.

## Fixed by

Three revisions of the `next` branch. They are in trunk since the merge
[r14650](https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/code/14650/).

- [r14555](https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/code/14555/): `optimizeValinfoNarrow` in
  `src/SDCCgenconstprop.cc` calls `optimizeMult` for `/` and `%` as well as for `*`, and
  `optimizeMult` narrows a 16-bit operation when the ranges of both operands fit in 8 bits. The
  mcs51 code generator then emits `div ab`.
- [r14556](https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/code/14556/): peephole rule 186.f in
  `src/mcs51/peeph.def` replaces the 16-bit addition of the table address with
  `mov dptr,#table` and `movc a,@a+dptr`.
- [r14559](https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/code/14559/): a peephole rule replaces `mov %1,a` and
  `mov %2,%1` with `mov %2,a` when `%1` is not used afterward.

## Related

The comments propose two more changes that trunk does not have. One is a peephole rule that turns
the decrement and test of an object into `djnz`. The other is a register allocator that keeps the
incremented value in `a`.

In the fifteenth comment a maintainer reports 2069 bytes for the program on the `next` branch. The
ticket gives 1972 bytes for 3.5.0 and states that the program must fit in 2 KB of flash.
